title: Canoe on Moraine Lake in Banff
description: Rock flour suspended in glacial meltwater gives that colour. Private vehicles are now banned on the Moraine Lake road - shuttle only.

title: Drive the Icefields Parkway to Jasper
description: 232km past more than 100 glaciers between Lake Louise and Jasper - routinely called one of the great drives anywhere.

title: Stargaze in Jasper's Dark Sky Preserve
description: One of the largest accessible dark sky preserves in the world, with a decent chance of aurora on clear winter nights.

title: Walk the sea floor at Hopewell Rocks
description: The highest tides on earth, up to 16m. You walk on the ocean floor at low tide and kayak over the same spot six hours later.

title: Drive the Cabot Trail in autumn
description: 298km around Cape Breton's highlands, through Acadian and Gaelic communities, at its best when the maples turn in early October.

title: See polar bears at Churchill
description: Bears gather here waiting for Hudson Bay to freeze. There is no road in - you arrive by train or plane, and go out in a tundra buggy.

title: Visit the Watchmen sites on Haida Gwaii
description: Standing mortuary poles at SGang Gwaay, guarded by Haida Watchmen and deliberately left to return to the earth. Access is permitted and limited.

title: Take the boat under Horseshoe Falls
description: Around 2,800 cubic metres a second go over the Horseshoe. The Canadian side has the view; the boat gets you into the spray.

title: Walk the walled old town of Quebec City
description: The only walled city north of Mexico, founded 1608, and the most convincingly European place in North America.

title: Drive the Dempster Highway to the Arctic Ocean
description: Around 900km of gravel from Dawson City to Tuktoyaktuk on the Arctic Ocean. Carry two spare tyres - this is not an exaggeration.

title: Cycle the Stanley Park seawall
description: A 9km flat loop around a 400-hectare forest on a downtown peninsula, past totem poles and under the Lions Gate Bridge.

title: Cross the Capilano Suspension Bridge
description: 137m of swaying cedar plank 70m above a river gorge, first strung across in 1889. The free Lynn Canyon bridge nearby does much the same job.

title: Eat your way around Granville Island Public Market
description: An industrial sandbar turned market and artist quarter under a bridge, reached by tiny rainbow-coloured ferries that hold about twelve people.

title: Drive the Sea to Sky Highway to Whistler
description: 120km along Howe Sound with the water on one side and granite on the other, past Shannon Falls and the Stawamus Chief.

title: Climb the Stawamus Chief at Squamish
description: One of the largest granite monoliths in the world, climbed by chains and ladders to three summits above Howe Sound.

title: Hike to the Joffre Lakes
description: Three stacked glacial lakes in improbable turquoise. Day passes are required, and the park now closes for periods so Lil'wat and N'Quatqua Nations can harvest.

title: Ride the Peak 2 Peak gondola at Whistler
description: The largest ski resort in North America, linked by a gondola with the longest unsupported span in the world at over 3km between towers.

title: Storm-watch at Tofino in winter
description: People book rooms specifically to watch Pacific storms hit Long Beach. Surfing here happens year-round in a thick wetsuit.

title: Walk the rainforest trails in Pacific Rim National Park
description: Old-growth Sitka spruce and western red cedar on boardwalks over bog, with the West Coast Trail running south for 75 gruelling kilometres.

title: See the Butchart Gardens near Victoria
description: Built inside an exhausted limestone quarry from 1904 onward by the cement magnate's wife, and now a national historic site.

title: Look for the spirit bear in the Great Bear Rainforest
description: The Kermode bear is a white-coated black bear found almost nowhere else - maybe 400 exist. Access is through First Nations-led operators only.

title: Taste ice wine in the Okanagan Valley
description: Canada's warmest wine region, on a desert lake, and the source of most of the world's ice wine - pressed from grapes frozen on the vine.

title: Paddle to Emerald Lake in Yoho
description: Takakkaw Falls drops 254m in the same park, and the Burgess Shale here holds the best-preserved Cambrian fossils found anywhere.

title: Canoe on Lake Louise beneath the Victoria Glacier
description: Get there before seven or the car park is full by eight. In winter the lake freezes hard enough to skate and they carve an ice castle on it.

title: Walk on the Athabasca Glacier at the Columbia Icefield
description: The largest icefield in the Rockies, feeding three oceans. Markers along the approach road show where the glacier stood each decade - it is a sobering walk.

title: Ride the gondola at Banff for the Bow Valley view
description: Up Sulphur Mountain to a boardwalk along the summit ridge, with hot springs at the bottom that started the whole national park system in 1885.

title: See the dinosaur collection at the Royal Tyrrell Museum
description: One of the largest dinosaur collections in the world, in Drumheller, because the badlands around it are among the richest fossil beds anywhere.

title: Walk the hoodoos at Dinosaur Provincial Park
description: World Heritage listed, and more than 400 dinosaur skeletons have come out of it - many still lie exposed where they eroded out.

title: Visit Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump
description: Blackfoot peoples drove bison off this cliff for nearly 6,000 years. The interpretive centre is built into the hillside and told from their perspective.

title: Walk the Red Rock Canyon in Waterton Lakes
description: Joined to Montana's Glacier as the world's first International Peace Park, where prairie runs straight into mountain with no foothills between.

title: Go to the Calgary Stampede
description: Ten days of rodeo, chuckwagon racing and pancake breakfasts every July, with the whole city in boots. Running since 1912.

title: Hear the silence in Grasslands National Park
description: A Dark Sky Preserve of mixed-grass prairie with reintroduced bison and black-tailed prairie dogs, and almost no light or noise for a hundred kilometres.

title: Snorkel with beluga whales at Churchill
description: Around 57,000 belugas move into the Churchill River estuary each summer. They are curious enough to come and inspect a snorkeller.

title: Do the EdgeWalk on the CN Tower
description: A hands-free walk on a 1.5m ledge around the outside of the tower at 356m, tethered to an overhead rail. The tallest such walk in the world.

title: Swim at the Grotto on the Bruce Peninsula
description: A limestone sea cave on Georgian Bay with water clear enough to be mistaken for the Caribbean, and roughly ten degrees colder than it looks.

title: Canoe and portage through Algonquin Park
description: 2,400 lakes linked by portage, with wolf howls answered on organised August nights and maples that turn the whole park red in late September.

title: Skate the Rideau Canal in Ottawa
description: 7.8km of frozen canal used as a commuter route, with beavertail pastry stands on the ice. Warming winters mean some years it barely opens at all.

title: Cruise the Thousand Islands
description: Actually 1,864 islands in the St Lawrence, split between Canada and the US - one holds the shortest international bridge in the world.

title: Eat a smoked meat sandwich and a bagel in Montreal
description: Boiled in honey water and baked in a wood oven, the Montreal bagel is a genuinely different thing from the New York version - and locals will explain why.

title: Walk up Mont Royal for the city view
description: Designed by Frederick Law Olmsted, who also did Central Park. Sunday afternoons in summer bring the tam-tams - an open drum circle on the east slope.

title: Stand at the foot of Montmorency Falls
description: 83m, higher than Niagara, with a suspension bridge across the lip and a via ferrata up the cliff beside it.

title: Watch belugas in the Saguenay Fjord
description: One of the longest fjords in the world outside Scandinavia, with a resident and endangered beluga population, plus blue whales at the confluence.

title: Walk to Perce Rock at low tide
description: A 400m limestone wall with an arch through it, walkable from shore at low tide, with the world's most accessible gannet colony on the island beyond.

title: Photograph the lighthouse at Peggy's Cove
description: A working fishing village on granite scoured bare by glaciers. People are swept off the black rocks near the water most years - stay on the light-coloured stone.

title: Walk the painted waterfront at Lunenburg
description: A World Heritage town laid out on a 1753 British grid, still in its original wooden buildings, and home port of the schooner on the Canadian dime.

title: Visit Green Gables on Prince Edward Island
description: The farmhouse that inspired Anne of Green Gables, on an island of red sand cliffs where the book still drives a good part of the economy.

title: Walk on the earth's mantle at the Tablelands
description: Peridotite from the earth's mantle, forced to the surface by continental collision. So toxic to plants that it looks like Mars - and it helped prove plate tectonics.

title: Boat into Western Brook Pond
description: A landlocked fjord with 600m walls, reached by a 3km bog walk before the boat. The water is so pure it barely conducts electricity.

title: Watch icebergs drift past Iceberg Alley
description: Ice calved off Greenland glaciers 10,000 years ago, drifting down the Labrador Current. Locals chip it out for gin, and there is a public tracking map.

title: Stand among the puffins at Elliston
description: One of the closest land-based puffin viewing sites in North America - the birds nest on a stack a few metres from where you stand.

title: See the Norse settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows
description: The only confirmed Norse site in North America, occupied around 1021 CE - five hundred years before Columbus, and dated precisely by a solar storm.

title: Climb Signal Hill above St John's
description: Where Marconi received the first transatlantic wireless signal in 1901, above a harbour entrance called the Narrows and a street of painted row houses.

title: Drink the Sourtoe cocktail in Dawson City
description: A gold rush town with wooden boardwalks and a bar that drops a mummified human toe into your drink. The rule is your lips must touch it.

title: Fly over the Kluane icefields
description: Canada's highest peak and the largest non-polar icefield on earth, almost none of it reachable on foot. The flightseeing run is the only realistic way in.

title: Raft past Virginia Falls in Nahanni
description: One of the first four sites ever added to the World Heritage list, in 1978. Virginia Falls is twice the height of Niagara, and access is by float plane only.

title: Watch the aurora from Yellowknife
description: Directly under the auroral oval with a flat horizon and very dry winter air - statistically among the most reliable aurora viewing anywhere on earth.

title: Reach the floe edge on Baffin Island
description: The line where sea ice meets open water, travelled by snowmobile and qamutik sled with Inuit guides - narwhal, bowhead and polar bear all use it.
